scenes.heading: Building a contract that protects your agency

sents.d: Building a contract that protects your agency
A clear scope of work prevents the most common client disputes in this field.

Social media management disputes often center on undefined scope — a client assumes 'managing social media' includes responding to every DM instantly, creating video content, and running ads, when the agreement only covered scheduled posts.

A contract should explicitly list which platforms are covered, posting frequency, what's included in community management (e.g. comments only, or DMs too), and whether content creation, paid ad management, and reporting are included or billed separately.

Including a termination clause with a required notice period (e.g. 30 days) protects your business from losing a retainer with no warning, and is a standard, expected term in ongoing service agreements.

take: Spell out platforms, frequency and what's included, plus notice.
